A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuronAl pruning work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original pruning experiments, language-modeling perplexities, zero-shot accuracies, runtime measurements, and calibration/selection ablations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds larger/newer-model evaluations, inference throughput measurements, and alignment-metric and calibration-source experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions select block-wise and then row-wise sparsity through normalized dense–sparse activation alignment, without retraining. SparseGPT already uses the block-only variant in v2. v4 specifies activation locations and rewrites the procedure, but does not establish a change to the intended pruning method.

E1.justification: Both use WikiText2, C4, PTB, and the same seven zero-shot tasks. Added model configurations, sparsity sweeps, calibration-source comparisons among these datasets, and throughput measurements expand evaluation settings without establishing new language-task or data coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds dense-model reference rows to existing comparisons and evaluates reconstruction-error, cosine, and KL variants in Table 13. The main Uniform/DSnoT/OWL/AlphaPruning comparator set is retained; BESA/DSA runtime comparisons and SparseGPT experiments were already present.

E3.justification: v4 adds Llama-2 70B and Llama-3 8B configurations, 10%–50% sparsity evaluations, calibration-source controls, and end-to-end CPU generation timing. Section 5.3 introduces geometric-mean accuracy-retention and perplexity-factor metrics. Original calibration sizes, lambda grids, and baseline hyperparameters are retained in Appendix C.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's schedule, lambda-selection, seed, and sample-count studies, v4 tests reconstruction error versus alignment and cosine/KL alternatives (Table 13), varies calibration-source datasets (Table 14), and examines low-to-high sparsity behavior (Appendix D.7). Lambda-selection plots also add reconstruction-error selections.

E5.justification: Both report mean and standard deviation across calibration seeds 0, 16, and 46 at 60%, 70%, and 80% sparsity. v4 revises numerical summaries and adds calibration-source summaries using the same reporting practice; it reports no increased run count or new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds dense references, aggregate summaries, 70B/Llama-3 results, larger-model zero-shot/runtime results, throughput, and new ablation outcomes. It removes v2 Table 17's 60%-sparse 13B perplexities and revises the 70% seed-ablation values: Phi-2/WikiText2 changes from 85.5±3.3 to 86.7±1.6. Most original benchmark scores remain; new results include AlphaPruning outperforming NeuronAl on 70B perplexity.

T1.justification: v4 corrects the retained-weight count to (1−s)|D|, defines aggregate metrics (Eqs. 7–8), and adds time/memory complexity derivations (Appendix B). Its explicit GetDist formula introduces a sign inconsistency: Eq. 4 decreases block sparsity with depth, contrary to the increasing schedule stated below it. No new theorem is established.

C1.justification: The adaptive, retraining-free alignment contribution and performance–runtime claim remain. The introduction extends the claimed scale from 13B to 70B and adds an explicit claim of up to approximately 20-fold faster sparsity allocation than the closest competitor at 70B.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly explains projection-input alignment through residual connections and LayerNorm, contrasting global alignment with local output reconstruction. New discussions interpret large-model results as a perplexity/zero-shot/runtime tradeoff and describe limited benefits at low sparsity. Some added superiority interpretations exceed the evidence in Tables 6 and 13.

D1.justification: v4 specifies activation-capture locations, block-wise activation disposal, and the inference backend, CPU, core count, and sequence lengths. Its pseudocode now updates the incumbent alignment score, consistent with v2's stated minimization. The code URL, calibration configuration, lambda grids, A100 hardware, and selected-lambda tables were already disclosed.

R1.justification: v4 adds the DeepSparse reference and removes Hoang and Liu (2023) and Cunegatti et al. (2024), which supported v2's connectivity rationale. Appendix A more explicitly positions input alignment against reconstruction-error pruning. Most related work remains unchanged after matching publication and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The methodology is substantially rewritten into overview, alignment, block, and row subsections. Experiments are reorganized into evaluation, aggregate comparison, efficiency, and ablation sections; setup moves partly to Appendix C, and the original appendix is reorganized across A–F. These changes extend beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: The two-column conference layout becomes a predominantly single-column TMLR layout. Algorithm 1 becomes the two-panel Figure 3, lambda-selection figures are redrawn with added comparison markers, and the calibration-size plot moves into the main text. Tables gain dense-reference rows and new aggregate, scalability, throughput, and ablation displays.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v4 adds direct tests of the alignment rationale, larger/newer-model and calibration-source evidence, measured inference efficiency, and clearer activation documentation. These improve empirical support and transparency. However, new superiority claims conflict with Tables 6/13, and Eq. 4 contradicts its stated sparsity schedule, limiting the net quality gain.
